Following the former works , we evaluate attack methods using the following metrics: 1) EM, the exact match ratio of predicted answers; 2) F1, the F1 score between the predicted answers and the gold answers. Lower EM and F1 mean better attack effectiveness; 3) Grammar error (GErr), the context grammatical error numbers given by LanguageTool following , we use the average value per 100 tokens due to various context lengths among datasets; 4) PPL, the average perplexity of all adversarial contexts given by a small sized GPT2 model  to measure their fluency . Lower values of GErr and PPL indicate better textual quality.
